Hi Alice — great conversation today, thanks for your time. Quick recap and proposal for the POC trial so we have aligned expectations: 

Summary of needs (what I heard):
- Multilingual support (English + ES/PT/FR/DE-heavy use cases) for customer-facing chat and content generation.
- High reliability on fallback when high-latency/throughput spikes occur.
- Success criteria tied to latency, cost per 1k tokens, and qualitative quality (NPS on responses / 80% pass on eval prompts).

Proposed POC (high level):
- 3-week trial (2-week active eval + 1-week wrap-up & tuning).
- Models to test: primary candidate: Llama 2 70B (quantized for cost) + fallback candidate: MPT-30B (faster on certain workloads).
- Evaluation plan: shared prompt set (we'll load into the POC_Metrics_Template.xlsx), automated token-level metrics + human review for 200 sample prompts across languages.
- Ownership: Redwood setup + infra (Ben & Rishi), Evaluation & qualitative review (Marissa), ACME point-of-contact: Alice / Tom.
- Deliverables: weekly checkpoint, end-of-POC findings (cost projection, recommended model, config & rollout plan).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the success criteria above (especially the languages and the 80% pass threshold).
2) Share any additional evaluation prompts (drop into the Drive link) by Tue 8/18 so Marissa can start drafting the test harness.
3) We'll send the SOW and network checklist for procurement this afternoon (see attachments).

Attachments: POC_Metrics_Template.xlsx, Redwood_POC_SOW.pdf

If that looks good I can schedule the infra kickoff for Monday and loop Rishi in to provision dedicated trial capacity.

Thanks,

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Alice's confirmation. Key asks and proposed internal plan: 

Primary model candidate: Llama 2 70B (4-bit quantized)
- Pros: best overall quality for our test prompts, good multilingual performance when fine-tuned / instruction-tuned.
- Cons: higher baseline token cost and GPU memory pressure.

Fallback candidate: MPT-30B / Mistral-class  based lighter variant
- Pros: lower latency & cost; useful as fallback when latency > threshold or when confidence is low.
- Cons: may underperform on some idiomatic Spanish/Portuguese prompts.

Multilingual approach:
- Round 1: test English + Spanish + Portuguese explicitly in week 1. Include 50 prompts per language across chat & generation.
- Round 2: add FR/DE if primary passes basic SLA.

Eval plan & ownership:
- Marissa: build the eval harness and human review rubric, run weekly QA and produce scoring (accuracy, relevance, hallucination count).
- Rishi: provision trial infra (dedicated trial nodes), enable KV-cache + prefix caching, and implement routing policy for fallback. Provide baseline perf numbers (p50/p95 latency) by EOD Wed.
- Ben: customer comms, coordinate procurement & SOW signatures.

Routing/fallback specifics to implement in trial:
- Latency-based: if p95 > 600ms on primary for 1 minute, route new requests to fallback for that customer tenant for 10 minutes.
- Confidence-based: use model perplexity/surprise heuristic + safety score; if below threshold, route to fallback and flag for human review.

Can you both confirm ownership and whether the Llama 2 70B (4-bit) + MPT-30B combo is feasible for the trial? If not, propose an alternative (e.g., Llama 2 13B tuned + MPT fallback) and I'll relay to Alice.

Thanks,
Ben
